source.title: The Greek podcast corpus: Competitive speech models for low-resourced languages with weakly supervised data
source.authors: Georgios Paraskevopoulos; Chara Tsoukala; Athanasios Katsamanis; Vassilis Katsouros

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses weakly supervised fine-tuning to build Greek ASR models and reports their performance, but it does not test whether the fine-tuned models beat the model that produced their labels or measure PGR.
record.gate_note: Whisper-large-v3 generates the silver transcriptions, but its WER is not reported on the evaluation sets used to compare the fine-tuned students. The reported comparisons are with the same students before fine-tuning and with Whisper-large-v2; there is no weak-supervisor comparison, strong true-label ceiling, or PGR.
record.test_reason: This is pseudo-label distillation for Greek ASR, not weak-to-strong generalization. The label producer (Whisper-large-v3, 1550M) is larger and stronger than the students (small 244M, medium 769M), so the supervisor/student size ordering is the reverse of every version. The study does not cite or use the weak-to-strong finding, and it reports no PGR or true-label ceiling.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that weakly supervised (pseudo-labelled) podcast corpora are a cost-effective way to train competitive Greek ASR models, with gains scaling with data and model size.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes Whisper-small and Whisper-medium for Greek ASR on Whisper-large-v3-generated transcripts. It does not use or report the original PGR comparison, a true-label ceiling, or the original task setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports performance varying with training-corpus size and across evaluation datasets and podcast domains.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller Whisper models fine-tuned on large-v3 silver transcripts sharply cut WER (small 42.87→12.16, medium 24.22→9.95 on GPC test). On CV, fine-tuned medium (12.8) beats its supervisor large-v3 (13.98). Elsewhere the students remain worse than large-v3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Strong-to-weak pseudo-label distillation: a smaller ASR student trained on a larger model's transcripts can occasionally match or beat the teacher on out-of-domain test sets.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuned students beat large-v2 across all 16 podcast domains and beat it from GPC-5 (60 h) upward. Large-v2 is not the label producer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weakly supervised in-domain fine-tuning lets smaller ASR models surpass a larger untuned model with modest data.

record.problems: The weak supervisor's evaluation performance and a true-label ceiling are not reported, so the paper cannot establish student-over-supervisor performance or PGR. The paper notes that Whisper-large-v3 was used to create GPC transcripts and therefore was not included in that evaluation. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported WER results.
record.rows_left_out: Per-domain and per-training-size numerical WER points from Figures 2 and 3 are not available in the supplied text; only the textual aggregate claims are recorded in r11 and r12.

untested.parts: No weak supervisor paired with a stronger student, and no PGR or ground-truth-trained ceiling.
No auxiliary loss, ensembling or loss variants.
No PGR versus supervisor or student size, and no representation predictors.
No supervisor-exploitation, distribution-shift PGR or error-similarity analysis.
Speech, not vision. No weak-to-strong setup in any case.

missing.what: Label-producer (Whisper-large-v3) WER on the out-of-training sets: Fleurs 11.02, CV 13.98, LG 10.86, HParl 16.99. No row records these, and they are the teacher comparison a researcher would need.

record.verdict_notes: The record's gate_note is wrong: large-v3 WER is reported in Table 3 for the four external corpora, though not on the GPC test set. The key reason this study does not test the claim is that the supervisor is stronger than the students. T4 is not apt either, because the tool relied on is self-training or pseudo-labelling, not the weak-to-strong finding.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare student performance with the weak supervisor or report PGR.
Does not compare auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling, or loss variants with naive fine-tuning.
Reports ASR results across model sizes, datasets, and training-set sizes, but not PGR, supervisor-size effects, or representation predictors.
Does not test supervisor-checking failures, distribution shift effects on PGR, or error similarity between supervisor and student.
No theoretical conditions are proposed or tested.
